questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: On a compressed gas tank, liquid discharge valves must be opened during loading and unloading. They should be closed at all other times.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the markings and labels on packages to the shipping papers. Check that the shipper wrote the correct description on the shipping paper and put the right labels on the packages.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained?

options.text: At least once every three years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years
questions.explanation: Employees who work with hazardous materials must be trained and tested at least once every three years.

questions.question: To choose the right placard, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The type of container holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: To pick the right placards, you must know the hazard class of the materials, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while carrying chlorine:

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must slow down before crossing the tracks.
You may cross the tracks without stopping if no warning lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: If carrying any amount of chlorine, always stop at a railroad crossing 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Stop whether or not you see a train.

questions.question: If hazardous materials in your vehicle catch fire, you should:

options.text: Try to put it out with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them fight the fire.
Hope the fire goes out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them fight the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire needs special training and equipment. Do not fight the fire yourself unless you have proper training and gear.

questions.question: The only way to correctly check tire pressure is:

options.text: By pressing on the tire with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only reliable way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Keep hazardous materials away from heat.

questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake before loading or unloading hazardous materials. Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers. Keep hazardous materials away from heat sources.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should not be:

options.text: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
Parked within 40 feet of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Never park it within five feet of the road edge.

questions.question: On a shipping paper with both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials may be identified by being:
questions.explanation: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous items must be clearly marked. They may be listed first, highlighted in a different color, or marked with an "X" before the description.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, what do they certify?

options.text: The package does not contain hazardous materials.
The package was prepared following all rules.
The package was packed at a different location.

questions.correctAnswerText: The package was prepared following all rules.
questions.explanation: A shipper of hazardous materials must certify on the shipping paper that the shipment was prepared according to all rules.

questions.question: What does a driver need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a tank endorsement
A CDL with a cargo endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: Shippers package materials in order to ____ hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to fully contain them. Vehicles must be placarded to show the danger of the cargo.

questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's identification number appear?

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.explanation: The material's ID number must appear on the shipping paper and on the packaging. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, how should the trailer be cleaned?

options.text: Left to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Parts of a vehicle exposed to corrosive liquids must be thoroughly washed with water.

questions.question: Where can hazardous materials shipping papers be kept?

options.text: In a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers should be kept in a pouch in the driver's side door or another location the driver can easily reach while wearing a seat belt. The papers must be clearly visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: What does a shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: Shipping papers must include a description of the specific hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: While driving, shipping papers should be:
questions.explanation: Shipping papers should be kept in a pouch in the driver's side door or another location the driver can easily reach while wearing a seat belt. The papers must be clearly visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: How must you complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest?

options.text: Only sign the manifest if you cross into another state.
Have a witness sign the manifest.

questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. The manifest must be signed by hand.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT your job as a driver at an accident scene?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene.
Trying to put the fire out yourself.
Telling emergency responders about the hazardous materials danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put the fire out yourself.
questions.explanation: If you have an accident with hazardous materials, keep people away, limit material spread if safe, tell emergency responders about the dangers, and give them shipping papers and emergency information. Do not try to fight hazardous materials fires unless you have protective equipment and training.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous materials are also flammable.

questions.question: If you see a cargo leak, how should you identify the hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: If you find a cargo leak, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Do not touch or smell leaking materials. This could cause injury or death.

questions.question: You should not smoke within ____ of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases) materials. Do not carry lit cigarettes, cigars, or pipes near vehicles with flammable or explosive materials.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: All drivers must be trained on hazardous materials safety and security risks. This training must happen at least once every three years and include testing.

questions.question: Who is responsible for marking and labeling materials for shipping?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for correctly labeling and marking hazardous materials. The driver should verify that materials are properly labeled and marked before starting the trip.

questions.question: You may leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended:

options.text: On the shoulder of a highway.

questions.explanation: You may only leave a vehicle with explosives unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: Which type of material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials must have a transport index. This is a number that shows how much control the material needs during transport. The total transport index in one vehicle cannot exceed 50.

questions.question: Which agency helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.explanation: The National Response Center coordinates emergency response to chemical hazards. Contact them if there is a hazardous materials spill.

questions.question: A placarded vehicle must have a fire extinguisher with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have a fire extinguisher with an Underwriters Laboratories (UL) rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: Placards must be placed:

options.text: Within three inches of other markings.
So words and numbers read from left to right.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed at least three inches away from other markings. Words and numbers must be level and read from left to right.
